Setup guide · Git2App · 1 Nov 2026

Set up Git2App so it can turn Xpenstack into store apps

The code is done. These are the accounts and settings only you can create. Do them in order, about 90 minutes in all. Everything is clicking and pasting in your web browser: no commands, no Git Bash, nothing to install. Steps marked "Claude can do this" I do as soon as you say go.

Your values

Type yours once. Every Copy button and link below uses them. The free Cloudflare addresses work fine; a domain of your own can come later.

Both addresses are on your own domain, xpenstack.com (1 Nov).

The whole flow

WebsiteCloudflare Pages. You sign in and tap Build.

↓ sign-in

SupabaseAccounts, apps list, build history, locked signing keys

↓ every action

APICloudflare Worker

↓ reads code

GitHub AppRead-only, only the repos you pick

↓ starts builds

GitHub ActionsFresh Linux (Android) or Mac (iPhone) per build
Cloudflare R2Stores the finished APK, AAB and IPA for 30 days

ABefore you start

Once, about 5 minutes.

  1. Turn on two-step sign-in for GitHub, Cloudflare and Supabase. Whoever gets into one of them can change what Git2App builds.

    Open GitHub securityOpen Cloudflare securityOpen Supabase security

  2. Open your password manager and make a new note called "Git2App". Every secret below goes into that note first, and then into the one place named. Never into a chat, a screenshot or an email.

BCreate the GitHub App people install

About 15 minutes. This is how Git2App reads a repo, read-only.

  1. Open the new GitHub App form.

    Open New GitHub App

  2. Fill in these boxes, one Copy at a time.

    GitHub App name
    Homepage URL
    Identifying and authorizing users › Redirect URI (GitHub used to call it Callback URL)
    Allow wildcard matchingleave unticked
    Expire user authorization tokensleave ticked
    Request user authorization (OAuth) during installationtick it
    Webhook URL
    Webhook secret: make one here, save it in your note, then paste itnot made yet

  3. Scroll to Permissions › Repository permissions. Set Contents to Read-only. Leave everything else on No access (Metadata turns to Read-only by itself).

  4. Scroll past the permission lists. Under Subscribe to events tick Push (it appears once Contents is on). Under Where can this GitHub App be installed? choose Only on this account. Tap Create GitHub App.

  5. On the page that opens, copy the App ID and Client ID into your note. Tap Generate a new client secret and copy it into your note too (GitHub shows it once).

    Before any screenshot: cover every long code GitHub says you "won't be able to see again". A secret in a screenshot has to be replaced.

    GitHub now keeps secrets and keys on their own page: left menu › Credentials, with two tabs, Client secrets and Key pairs.

    Screenshot slot: the Client secrets section, with the secret covered.

  6. Left menu › Credentials › Key pairs tab › New key. A file ending in .private-key.pem downloads to your Downloads folder. Leave it there. You don't change it in any way: in section G you open it in Notepad and copy what's inside.

Change (1 Nov): the addresses moved to xpenstack.com after these screenshots were taken. The screenshots still show the old pages.dev and workers.dev addresses: always use the Copy buttons, which have the new ones.

CCreate the Workers App (only for this repo)

About 10 minutes. It lets the API start and stop builds here, so people never give Git2App access to their own Actions.

  1. Open the form again and fill in:

    Open New GitHub App
    GitHub App name
    Homepage URLhttps://github.com/shubhamrkrock/PWA-to-app-converter
    Webhookuntick Active
    Repository permissionsActions: Read and write
    Where can it be installedOnly on this account

  2. Tap Create GitHub App. Copy its App ID into your note. Then left menu › Credentials › Key pairs › New key. A second .private-key.pem file downloads, with "workers" in its name. Leave it in Downloads too.

  3. In the left menu tap Install App › Install › Only select repositories › PWA-to-app-converter › Install. The address of the page you land on ends in a number: that is the installation id. Copy it into your note.

    Screenshot slot: the address bar ending in the installation id.

DTwo settings in this repo

About 5 minutes.

  1. Add the variable that tells builds which API they may talk to. Tap New repository variable.

    Open Actions variables
    NameG2A_API_ORIGIN
    Value (no slash at the end)

    Change the address later (1 Nov): on the same page, https://github.com/shubhamrkrock/PWA-to-app-converter/settings/variables/actions, with Actions selected on the left, tap the pencil next to G2A_API_ORIGIN, paste the new value and tap Update variable.

  2. Add the signing environment. Tap New environment, name it, then under Deployment branches and tags choose Selected branches and tags and add main. Add no secrets to it.

    Open Environments
    Environment nameg2a-signing

Public repo, so read this (31 Oct): the repo is public for free build minutes. That means anyone can read build logs, and for one day download a release build's unsigned app. For your own Xpenstack that is fine: its web code is public on its website anyway. Before other people use Git2App, builds must move to a private repo (paid minutes) or another build service.

ESupabase: the accounts database

Done 1 Nov. Shared with your Minutes project, now named "Git2App and Minutes", because the free plan allows only two projects.

Claude did the database part: all Git2App tables, the security rules, and your account on the pro plan. Sign-in is invite-only in this project (a Minutes rule), so new Git2App users need an invite first.

  1. Sign-in keys: nothing to change. The current key is already the newer kind, ECC (P-256). Leave the "Previous" HS256 key alone, Minutes may still use it.

    Open JWT Keys

    Page link: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt/settings/jwt

  2. Return addresses. Leave Site URL as it is (Minutes uses it). Under Redirect URLs tap Add URL, paste, save.

    Open URL Configuration

    Page link: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt/auth/url-configuration

    Redirect URLhttps://git2app.xpenstack.com/projects

  3. Later, in step G, you copy the service_role key from the API keys page into Cloudflare. It is a full-access secret: copy it straight from Supabase into Cloudflare, never into a chat.

    Open API keys

    Page link: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt/settings/api-keys

Mistake we hit (1 Nov): Supabase's approval pop-up for a database change never reached the phone, so the change timed out. Fix: Claude gives the SQL, you paste it in the SQL editor and tap Run.

Rename (optional, label only): https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt/settings/general

Skipped for now (1 Nov): you sign in with an email link. Come back to this later.

  1. GitHub sign-in. Create an OAuth app (a different thing from the GitHub App in B).

  2. Paste that Client ID and secret into Supabase's GitHub provider and switch it on.

    Open Sign In providers

  3. Google sign-in. In Google Cloud, set up the consent screen (External, app name Git2App, your email), then create an OAuth client of type Web application.

GThe API on Cloudflare

About 20 minutes, all in the Cloudflare website. The code is on main (1 Nov), so you can start.

Claude already did the file part. Your addresses (xpenstack.com) and app name are in the API's settings file.

  1. Done 1 Nov. Storage for finished apps: R2 switched on (free up to 10 GB, $0 a month), and Claude made the bucket git2app-artifacts.

    Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/r2/overview

  2. Done 1 Nov. Two job queues. Create Queue, paste the name, leave Jurisdiction on None, Create. Then the second one.

    Open Queues

    Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/queues

    First queuegit2app-dispatch
    Second queuegit2app-dispatch-dlq

  3. Put the API online as a Worker. Open Create a Worker and tap Continue with GitHub (the GitHub cat with the green dot). If Cloudflare asks for GitHub access, allow only PWA-to-app-converter. Pick that repo, fill in the boxes below, and send Claude a screenshot before tapping Deploy.

    Open Create a Worker

    Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers-and-pages/create

    Project namegit2app-api
    Build commandnpm ci
    Deploy commandnpx wrangler deploy --config apps/api/wrangler.toml
    Path (root directory)leave empty
    Production branchmain

    Mistake we hit (1 Nov): "Continue to Pages" at the bottom leads to Pages (address ends in /create/pages). That is for the website in step H, not the API. Tap ‹ Create a Worker to go back.

    Mistake we hit (1 Nov): the repo list showed only Xpenstack and MeetingAgent, because Cloudflare's GitHub app was only allowed those. Fix: open https://github.com/settings/installations, tap Configure next to Cloudflare Workers and Pages, under Repository access › Select repositories add PWA-to-app-converter, tap Save. Then go back to Cloudflare and reload the page.

    The form comes pre-filled with Cloudflare's guesses. Replace every box: Cloudflare fills the project name from the repo (pwa-to-app-converter), but it must be git2app-api, the same as the API's settings file, or the build fails.

    Preview commandnpx wrangler versions upload --config apps/api/wrangler.toml
    Enable Preview buildsturn it off

    Before Deploy, open Advanced settings under the form: Path stays /; API token stays Create new token (Cloudflare makes a build token for this Worker only); give it a name you'll recognise, or leave the name empty (Cloudflare then names it itself: "A new token will be created automatically"); leave Variable name and value empty, because the secrets go into the Worker's settings in the next step, not here.

    API token namegit2app-api-build

    After you tap Deploy, a spinner says "Setting up your repository. This may take a few seconds...". Wait; don't tap anything or close the page.

    After about a minute the build page shows a green tick next to Build and all five steps (Initializing, Cloning, Installing, Building, Deploying) green. Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/services/view/git2app-api/production/deployments

    Then tap the Domains tab (open it): it should list git2app-api.xpenstack.com (Cloudflare makes it itself).

    Leave both workers.dev switches off: the API should only answer on your own address. Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/services/view/git2app-api/production/domains

  4. Add the secrets. Open the new git2app-api Worker › Settings › Variables and Secrets › Add variable (top right of "Runtime variables and secrets"). The "Add environment variable" form opens. Keep Production ticked and Previews unticked. For each row of the table below: paste the name into Key, tick Secret first, then paste the value into Value. Tap + Add for the next row. When all 13 rows are in, tap Add variable and deploy once. The private keys may lose their line breaks when pasted; that is fine, the app reads them anyway.

    Open the Worker's settings

    Page link: https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/services/view/git2app-api/production/settings. Six plain variables (API_ORIGIN, CREDENTIALS_KEY_REF, GITHUB_APP_SLUG, WEB_ORIGIN, WORKERS_REF, WORKERS_REPO) and two bindings (ARTIFACTS, DISPATCH_QUEUE) are already there: the build put them in from the repo. Don't edit or delete them; you only add the 13 secrets below.

    Mistake we hit (1 Nov): the first row was filled but Secret was not ticked. Tick it on every row before you deploy.

    NameValue from
    SUPABASE_URL https://ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt.supabase.co
    SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY Supabase › Project Settings › API Keys › Legacy API keys tab › service_role › Reveal › Copy. Open it

    Where the SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY value is. Page link: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/ogmtlwfqfcztrobsyezt/settings/api-keys/legacy. Use the service_role row (marked "secret"), not the anon row.

    GITHUB_APP_ID 5567913 (App page)
    GITHUB_CLIENT_ID Starts with Iv, near the top of the App page
    GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET The App page shows a client secret only once, right after Generate a new client secret (it then says "Added now", "Never used"): copy it then, into your note and here. Your note from B. Not saved? On the App page tap Generate a new client secret and copy it straight away
    GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET Not a file. It is the random text you made with the Make one button in step B and pasted into the GitHub App's Webhook secret box; it should be in your password note. GitHub never shows it again. Not in your note? Make a new one here, save it in your note, paste it on the App page › Webhook secret › Save changes, then use the same text here. Page link: https://github.com/settings/apps/git2app-shubham

    Mistake we hit (1 Nov): on the App page the Webhook URL still showed the old git2app-api.shubhamrkrock.workers.dev address. While you are there, change it to the value below, tap Change secret under it, paste the new webhook secret into the box that opens, and tap Save changes at the bottom.

    Webhook URLhttps://git2app-api.xpenstack.com/api/v1/github/webhooks
    New webhook secretnot made yet

    Not sure which text in your note is the webhook secret? Don't guess: tap Make one just above, tap Copy, paste it into your note on a new line that starts GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET =, then paste the same text into GitHub's Secret box and into Cloudflare. Tip: label every value in your note with its exact name from this table.

    GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY The first .pem file: see the next step
    WORKERS_APP_ID 5568119
    WORKERS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY The "workers" .pem file: see the next step
    WORKERS_INSTALLATION_ID 177546203
    STATE_SECRET Make one below
    TICKET_SECRET Make one below
    CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY Make one below

    Mistake we hit (1 Nov): three rows were left empty (GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET and the two private keys) because it was not clear where they come from. Client secret: the one GitHub showed once after Generate a new client secret; if it was not copied, generate another on the App page and delete the unused one. Private keys: see the next step (.pem files in Downloads, or Generate a private key on each App page at https://github.com/settings/apps).

    State secretnot made yet
    Ticket secretnot made yet
    Master key: keep it in your note forever. Lose it and saved signing keys can't be opened.not made yet

    Screenshot slot: the Add variable form with Type set to Secret (value covered).

  5. How to copy a .pem file's inside. Open File Explorer (the yellow folder on the taskbar) › Downloads. Right-click the .private-key.pem file › Open with › Notepad (if Notepad isn't listed: Choose another app › Notepad). Press Ctrl+A to select everything, then Ctrl+C to copy. Paste it as the secret's value. It starts with -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----; copy all of it, nothing changed.

    Which file goes where: git2app-shubham.<date>.private-key.pem → GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY; git2app-shubham-workers.<date>.private-key.pem (the one with "workers" in its name) → WORKERS_APP_PRIVATE_KEY.

    When both keys are in Cloudflare, delete the two .pem files from Downloads and empty the Recycle Bin.

HThe website on Cloudflare Pages

About 10 minutes.

  1. Open Workers & Pages › Create › Pages › Import an existing Git repository and pick PWA-to-app-converter.

    Open Create Pages

  2. Fill in the build settings.

    Project namegit2app
    Production branchmain
    Framework presetNone
    Build commandnpm ci && npm run build:web
    Build output directoryapps/web/dist

  3. Open Environment variables and add three. None of them is a secret.

    VITE_SUPABASE_URL
    VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEYthe anon key from E
    VITE_API_ORIGIN

    Screenshot slot: the three variables.

  4. Tap Save and Deploy. When it says Success, open the site.

    It opens on a git2app.pages.dev address first. The next step moves it to yours.

  5. Put it on your domain. In the git2app Pages project › Custom domains › Set up a custom domain, paste the name, tap Continue, then Activate domain. Cloudflare adds the DNS record itself because xpenstack.com is in the same account. It can take a few minutes to show Active.

    Custom domaingit2app.xpenstack.com
    Open the website

ICheck it works

  1. Sign in on the website. Go to GitHub › Connect GitHub and install your GitHub App on Xpenstack only.

  2. Go to Apps › New app › Xpenstack › branch dev › Add and check it. In a few minutes the check report shows Android and iPhone verdicts.

  3. Fill in Settings, then Build › Android › Testing on my phone. When it says Ready, download the APK on your Android phone.

  4. Something red? Copy the message and send it to me.

Mistakes we hit

  

    
What happenedFix

    
      
Checks never started; jobs showed no runner (31 Oct)Private repo had used its free minutes. Made the repo public, so builds are free

      
The iPhone test showed "skipped"It only runs when started by hand with "ios" ticked, by design

      
The GitHub App form had no "Callback URL" box (1 Nov)GitHub renamed it: paste it into Redirect URI

      
A screenshot sent in chat showed the webhook secret (1 Nov)Make a new one before creating the app; cover secret boxes before taking a screenshot

      
No "Private keys" or "Client secrets" on the General page (1 Nov)GitHub moved them: left menu › Credentials, tabs Client secrets and Key pairs

      
A screenshot showed the new client secret (1 Nov)Tap New secret again, save the new one, Delete the old one

      
The guide asked for Git Bash commands to convert keys and store secrets (1 Nov)Removed: Git2App now reads the key file as GitHub gives it, and everything is done by clicking in the Cloudflare website

      
Bare addresses in replies weren't tappableEvery link is now a button or a full link
